Clinical Overview

High-Speed Vibration Therapy Designed for Fast, Focused Clinical Use

The NerveSpa Vibe is a high-frequency vibration tool designed to help clinicians target deep tissue, joint regions, and nerve-rich areas with short, focused sessions. With output up to approximately 7,000 rpm, the Vibe supports neuropathy, scar tissue release, muscle tension reduction, joint mobility work, and recovery-oriented soft-tissue care.

Its compact cordless form makes it easy to use around treatment tables, chairs, and rehab spaces without adding complexity to the visit. Four color-coded speed levels, a built-in 10-minute auto timer, and a rechargeable lithium battery support repeatable sessions that can be standardized across care pathways.

Clinical Applications

Versatile Across Neuropathy, Mobility, Scar Tissue, and Recovery Protocols

 Neuropathy programs – vibration to feet, calves, and hands to support comfort and circulation.
 Scar tissue and adhesions – focused vibration over restricted fascial planes.
 Joint mobility – peri-joint soft tissue for stiffness and reduced range of motion.
 Myofascial trigger points and muscle tension – localized high-frequency vibration.
 Warm-up or cool-down adjunct – useful for rehab and performance programs.

Key Focus Areas: Neuropathy support • Scar tissue & adhesions • Joint mobility • Trigger points • Recovery & warm-up

High-Frequency Vibration Features

Compact, Cordless, and Built for Repeatable Short Sessions

 High-Speed Output – four speed settings up to ~7,000 rpm for gentle to intense deep-tissue vibration.
 Color-Coded Speed Levels – Blue ~4,000 rpm, Green ~5,000 rpm, Yellow ~6,000 rpm, Red ~7,000 rpm.
 Compact & Cordless – lightweight one-hand form factor for easy movement around the table or chair.
 10-Minute Auto Timer – helps standardize session length and preserve battery life.
 Interchangeable Attachment Heads – supports both broad and pinpoint contact across different tissue targets.
 Pressure Overload Protection – helps protect the motor when excessive pressure is applied.

Clinical Pathways

Designed for Use In Clinic and as Part of Home-Care Continuity

Neuropathy Support

Apply high-frequency vibration to plantar surfaces, calves, or hands for short intervals as part of a broader neuropathy program that may also include electrotherapy, foot bath, and lifestyle support. This pathway is aimed at supporting comfort, circulation, and sensory awareness.

Joint Mobility & Range of Motion

Use around knees, shoulders, hips, ankles, and wrists to relax peri-articular soft tissues prior to mobilization, stretching, or exercise. This may help patients move more comfortably into loaded positions or rehab activities.

Scar Tissue & Adhesions

Focused vibration may be used along surgical scars or chronic adhesions, when clinically appropriate, to help loosen stiff fascial layers and improve tissue glide. This can be combined with manual therapy and stretching.

Trigger Points & Muscle Tension

Pinpoint attachment heads allow targeted work on myofascial trigger points in the neck, shoulders, low back, and extremities—especially when time is limited and the goal is fast, localized tissue preparation or relief.

Note: All protocols are determined by the supervising clinician and should be adapted to individual patient tolerance, comorbidities, and the overall care plan. Avoid direct use over the carotid sinus, eyes, open wounds, or any areas contraindicated for vibration or manual therapy.

Near implanted electronic devices (such as pacemakers or defibrillators).

source.question: Can TENS speed up healing or does it only mask pain?
source.answer: TENS is primarily used for pain relief, not to directly heal injuries. It helps by changing how pain signals are processed by the nervous system, which can make discomfort more manageable. By reducing pain, TENS may help some people move more comfortable, particupate in physical therapy, and stay active, which can support the overall recovery process. However, it does not repair damaged tissue or speed up healing on its own.

source.question: I am experiencing skin irritation -- why is that?
source.answer: Skin irriation after using a TENS unit is usually caused by skin sensitivity, electrode adhesive, or improper pad use. Common causes include: Sensitivity to the electrode gel or adhesive: Some people may have mild skin reactions to the materials in the pads. Using pads for too long: Extended use in the same area can irritate the skin. Worn or dirty electrodes: Old pads may not distribute stimulation evenly and can increase irritation. Applying pads to unprepared skin: Lotions, oils, sweat, or dirt can affect adhesion and skin comfort. Stimulation intensity is too high: Excessive intensity may cause discomfort or irritation. To reduce irritation: Apply pads to clean, dry skin. Rotate pad placement between sessions. Avoid using pads on irritated, broken, or sensitive skin. Lower the intensity if the sensation feels uncomfortable. Replace pads when they become dry or worn.

The electrical stimulation from a TENS unit typically does not affect non-electronic metal implants.
